svg.title: The Negotiation Table Decision Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-negotiation-table-gates; chapter number: 5; title: The Negotiation Table Decision Gates; subtitle: Questions contractors clear before conceding a dollar to an adjuster; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is the adjuster's extra demand a requirement rather than a recommendation?; pass next: Ask what the requirement is based on, then move to G2; fail action: Decline it plainly, as Chris Zimmerman puts it, I don't need this, and therefore I won't be doing it; gate: G2; question: Is the discussion limited to scope and pricing, not coverage?; pass next: Move to G3; fail action: Stop; coverage negotiation needs a license, and in Texas section 4102.163 voids power-of-attorney workarounds (Avner Gat, Daly and Black); gate: G3; question: Has the carrier estimate been read for squares, tear-off quantities and unit errors?; pass next: Move to G4; fail action: Rebuild the baseline first; catch errors like 24.48 SF entered for 2,448 SF, since a weak estimate creates a weak starting point (claimhelpme); gate: G4; question: Is the requested reduction 10% or less on a 3 to 4 minute question-list call?; pass next: Accept and collect; no claim is closed until all repairs are made and paid for (Chad Michael); fail action: Refuse reductions over 10% and collect the undisputed amount (Shane O'Dazier); caption: Frontline paid about $40,000 against an almost $75,000 bid, so the first carrier number is a baseline to attack, not accept.; assumptions note: Gate order is a sequencing of separate practitioner rules. The 10% ceiling is Shane O'Dazier's, and the trade-code switch from DMO reached about 40% approval for Chad Michael.; note: Attributed to Chris Zimmerman, Daly and Black P.C., Avner Gat Inc., claimhelpme, Builder's Perspective Public Adjusting, Shane O'Dazier and Chad Michael.

gate: G3; question: Has the carrier estimate been read for squares, tear-off quantities and unit errors?; pass next: Move to G4; fail action: Rebuild the baseline first; catch errors like 24.48 SF entered for 2,448 SF, since a weak estimate creates a weak starting point (claimhelpme)

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is a sequencing of separate practitioner rules. The 10% ceiling is Shane O'Dazier's, and the trade-code switch from DMO reached about 40% approval for Chad Michael.
